purpose: Execute the overturn_protocol's 'baseline + DVC 3.67.1' arm end to end in a scratch repo over the fixture data materialized by the project's own baseline tooling (blueprints/us-equities/nanosecond-replay/replay.py materialize), comparing restore fidelity after deletion with the baseline arm (project hash-manifest alone, no restore mechanism), to close identity-provenance gap 0 (DVC never installed/run) and gap 1 (does a DVC-tracked snapshot preserve the project hash-manifest contract, i.e. snapshot_sha256 and per-file hashes, after a restore).
preregistered: If DVC 3.67.1 can init/add/checkout the materialized fixture and, after the tracked directory is deleted, `dvc checkout` restores files whose sha256 exactly matches the pre-delete sha256 (including the manifest's own recorded snapshot_sha256/per-file hashes in snapshot.json), that settles gap 1's byte-identical-restore metric for the DVC arm. If the baseline arm's own scripts (replay.py, temporal_snapshot.py) contain no restore/backup/checkout logic, that establishes the baseline arm has zero restore capability of its own (only fail-closed detection via hash mismatch), which is the comparison basis the overturn_protocol asks for. A restore that does not match the pre-delete hashes, or a DVC failure, would refute the DVC arm as a fix for gap 0/1.

installs.name: dvc
installs.sha256: not individually recorded; installed via `uv pip install dvc==3.67.1` without --require-hashes (no pre-existing lock file for dvc's own dependency tree); dvc --version confirmed 3.67.1 post-install

result: DVC 3.67.1 init/add/status/checkout executed end to end in a new scratch repo (git+dvc) over the project's own materialized fixture output, in a new, never-before-existing prefix. After deleting the tracked directory, `dvc checkout` restored all 4 files (source.json, observations.parquet, universe.parquet, snapshot.json) byte-identical to the pre-delete state (sha256 diff empty, including the manifest's own recorded snapshot_sha256/per-file hashes in snapshot.json). Separately, grepping the baseline-arm scripts (replay.py, temporal_snapshot.py) for restore/backup/checkout/recover logic found zero matches: the baseline arm alone has no restore mechanism of its own; it can only fail-closed reject a corrupted/missing/tampered file via sha256 comparison (already covered by tests.test_nanosecond_replay.test_manifest_or_parquet_mutation_rejected and tests.test_point_in_time.test_parquet_corruption_and_wrong_manifest_hash_are_rejected), not recover the lost data. Services/processes added by the DVC arm: 1 additional CLI tool (dvc, no background daemon) plus a local `.dvc/cache` content-addressed store; no network remote was configured (fully local scratch repo). License: DVC is Apache-2.0 (per PyPI project metadata for dvc 3.67.1).

verdict_impact.explanation: Gap 0 said DVC's native_workflow was 'Prospective/UNEXECUTED' -- it is now executed here with a measured byte-identical restore. Gap 1 asked whether a DVC-tracked snapshot preserves the project hash-manifest contract after restore; it does (sha256 diff empty, snapshot_sha256 unchanged). This is evidence in favor of promoting the DVC arm from source-review-only toward measured for the identity-provenance decision (the current_choice's rationale explicitly rested on DVC being unexecuted), though PyIceberg and ArcticDB arms remain unrun and gap 4/5 (real licensed universe, remote licensing terms) stay open and needs_paid_entitlement, so this does not by itself close the whole layer decision.

limitations: Tested on a small synthetic fixture (5 observation rows, 2 universe rows), not at the scale of a real historical dataset; DVC's restore performance/fidelity at scale was not measured.

No remote (S3/GCS/etc.) was configured; only local cache-based checkout was tested, so remote-storage restore fidelity and gap 5's licensing-terms question for a private DVC remote remain untested and are recorded separately as needs_paid_entitlement (not in this unit's scope).
PyIceberg 0.12.0 and ArcticDB v6.26.0 arms from the same overturn_protocol were not run; this receipt speaks only to the DVC arm.
dvc's own dependency tree was installed without --require-hashes (no pre-existing lock covers DVC's ~60 transitive dependencies); only the top-level dvc==3.67.1 pin was verified via `dvc --version`.
